restrictions: One browser, one machine, one configuration: Firefox 10.0 (build 20120129021758) on Windows 2000 build 2195 without service pack, in a VirtualBox VM with 168 MB of RAM, a new profile and the preferences of validation/procedures/web.md. Under the PoC rule this stands for newer browsers; no other browser, version or operating system was run for the JavaScript path (Firefox 4 to 9, Chrome 15, Safari 5.1 and Opera 11.5 of spike S5 are untested), and Internet Explorer up to 9 is dropped by the owner (no typed arrays; spike S5).

History of the field: in the first series of 2026-11-15 (page with an <input type="text">) 14 of the 15 vectors passed and control_characters failed on its line feed, which a single-line field removes from its value in every browser (a current Chrome 157 does the same). By the owner's decision the field is now a one-row <textarea> (wrap off, maxlength 1000), and the second series passes all 15 vectors, control_characters included ('a', tab, line feed, 'b', U+0001 greeted unchanged). The first series is kept as it was (its evidence is listed as 'first series'); the node harness stub now normalises a textarea value (CRLF to LF) as a browser does.

The page was loaded over HTTP from the host through the VirtualBox NAT (http://10.0.2.2:<port>/), not from file:// and not from the Internet; the probe record was read from the page through an XMLHttpRequest POST (post=1, added to ui/legacy/web/app.js for browsers without a console or DOM dump), not from the title or the console. Each vector started a new firefox.exe, with the Firefox program files already in the guest's memory cache; display_ms (page start to greeting, 124 to 143 ms in the first series, 127 to 230 ms in the second) and the 704 to 843 ms (first series) and 520 to 1415 ms (second series) from the start of firefox.exe to the posted record are those of this VM, not of a cold start on real hardware.

Typing was exercised through the virtual keyboard of VirtualBox (keyboardputscancode), not by a person; the greeting was read from a screenshot. Tab into an <input> selects its text but Tab into a textarea does not, and on the French AZERTY layout of the guest the letter A is the key at scancode 0x10 (0x1E is Q): the first run of tools/trials/web-firefox-10-windows-2000-x86/typing-check-textarea.py sent Ctrl+0x1E, so 'Marie' was typed in front of 'Coucou' ('MarieCoucou', 'Bonjour MarieCoucou', screenshot discarded, log kept as typing-check-textarea-log.txt). The driver now sends Ctrl+0x10 and the retake shows the field 'Marie' and the greeting 'Bonjour Marie' (screenshot).
peak_rss_kb is null in every record: Firefox 10 has no performance.memory, so the memory was not measured (the probe schema allows null).

Not run: the WebAssembly path on this browser (Firefox 10 has no WebAssembly, so the page always takes the JavaScript path here), the 4,096-character texts typed (they were given through the URL and cut to 1,000 UTF-16 units by the page), the 1,000-character limit by keyboard, IME, clipboard, a high contrast scheme, a dark theme (prefers-color-scheme is not supported by Firefox 10), zoom and DPI above 96, slow-script warnings (none appeared: the page start takes about 0.1 s).

The VM was found PAUSED by the host power management (VBoxManage 'VM is paused due to host power management', paused since 2026-11-15T10:06Z, resume refused); a 'controlvm savestate' attempt made the VM process abort (state 'aborted'), so, as the owner's instruction allows for an unusable VM, the snapshot 'Claude Firefox 10' was restored ('snapshot restorecurrent') and the VM started again (gui). The guest state before the abort was lost; nothing in it was needed. No snapshot was taken, deleted or renamed.

End-of-life notice (owner decision 2026-11-15): the page now shows the notice on Windows 2000 (user agent 'Windows NT 5.0') and eol_warning_shown is true in all 15 records of the second series; the rule is the backend's (Windows below NT 11.0 is end of life) and the page only reads the system version from the user agent. It cannot tell Windows 10 from 11 and knows no version for macOS, Linux or Android, so there it never shows the notice (platform record, eol_note). The notice was seen on the screen of Firefox 10 in the one screenshot taken of the textarea check (see the notes).

Scope of this verdict (owner decision 2026-11-15): Chrome does not run on Windows 2000, so Firefox 10.0 alone stands for the Web Legacy ladder under the PoC rule and no Chrome or WebAssembly verdict is recorded. The WebAssembly path is exercised only by the node harness (run_vectors.py web-node-wasm, 15 of 15) and by one headless Chrome check (task T085), which are not verdicts.

Launch reliability of the second series: in this 168 MB guest a start of firefox.exe is lost about once in fifteen (the page is never requested: no line in the server log). Three attempts at the series each lost one start (right_to_left_arabic, ascii and emoji_zwj_sequence: 'no probe record posted in 120 s', 14 of 15) and were not stored; the launcher (tools/run_vectors.py, WEB_START_WAIT) now ends the processes and starts firefox.exe once more when the page was not requested after 30 s, and says so in the log: the stored series lost one start (accented) and passed after the second. VirtualBox also refused 'Maximum number of concurrent guest sessions (32)' once, because every `guestcontrol start` leaves a session open; `VBoxManage guestcontrol <vm> closesession --all` (no snapshot, no state change) cleared it.
disabled_features: peak-memory (Firefox 10 has no performance.memory: peak_rss_kb is null in every record; the page does not list it in the probe's disabled_features, which are empty)
